dmp.description:
Despite advances in chemotherapy and immunotherapy, melanoma remains a leading cause of cancer-related deaths in the European Union [1]. Localized photodynamic therapy and photothermal therapy (PTT) are promising non-invasive approaches for cancer treatment, relying on the use of a photosensitizer (PS) to absorb light [2]. Advanced nanotools such as gold nanoparticles, graphene oxide, transition metal dichalcogenides, black phosphorus, and some organic nanosystems have shown potential as effective PS agents for PTT due to their light-responsive properties [3]. Compared with traditional chemo/radiotherapy, PTT has fewer side effects and can selectively and effectively ablate tumor cells without harming surrounding tissue. However, challenges remain in the clinical application of PTT, such as the lack of effective targeting delivery strategies and the potential side effects of current photosensitizers. These limitations must be addressed before PTT can be widely adopted as a clinical therapeutic modality for melanoma and other cancers.
We hypothesized, that targeting delivery of novel nanolaminates, MXenes, loaded with specific anti-cancer antibodies could overcome current limitation in development of effective and safe photo-thermal strategy for melanoma treatment.
Based on the state of the art and our previous experience, the project scope is the development of a new effective anticancer treatment strategy based on the targeted PTT effect using innovative 2D materials coupled with specific monoclonal antibodies against melanoma cells.
To achieve the goals of this project, we have assembled an interdisciplinary team from Latvia University with expertise in medicine (oncology), pharmacology, nanotechnology, and cell biology. This project will be conducted in collaboration with the Horizon Europe project, "Towards MXenes' biomedical applications by high-dimensional immune MAPping," and with support from leading researchers in immunology and nanotechnology from Italy and the USA. Early-stage researchers (ERS) at the bachelor's and Ph.D. levels will be involved in the project to receive intensive interdisciplinary training that will enhance their employability and competitiveness in the job market.
The new knowledge generated by this project will be disseminated among the research, public, and business communities to raise awareness of the potential of PTT as a novel approach to cancer treatment and to pave the way for the translation of this approach into clinical practice. The ultimate goal of this project is to contribute to the development of effective, safe, and targeted therapies for melanoma and other types of cancer, thus improving the lives of patients and their families.
